newsitem.title: JAPAN: No plan to use more public money for bad loans - MOF.
newsitem.headline: No plan to use more public money for bad loans - MOF.

text.p: Japan has no plans to use more public funds to help resolve the bad loan problems at financial institutions, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters on Tuesday.

Asked whether the Finance Ministry had any plans to use fresh public funds to tackle the bad loan issue at financial institutions, Mitsuzuka said the government's decision not to do so remained unchanged.
On Monday, a key member of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party was reported to have said he was in favour of using more public money to help resolve the bad loan problem.
Mitsuzuka said: "We have stated that we will not use public funds for the bad loan problems at nonbank financial institutions. It is the same for other institutions."
He added that financial institutions needed to cut costs to improve their financial health.
Mitsuzuka also said the bad loan situation at nonbanks affiliated with banks had steadily been improving, as had the situation at banks themselves.
